_doc: Large batch L02 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10). Bears (black, sloth, ice, glacier), raccoons (raccoon, crab-eating), honey badger, aardvark, giant anteater, beaver foreman. New motifs live in motifs/large_L02.js (29, glyph/motion ids prefixed L02-, 7 custom chain effects); reused: honey-paw, ice-floe-slab, yakcalf-breath, cub-belly-slide, bin-clang, loose-skin (same pictures). Every piece (unique and class) has a hand note. All 10 signature motifs are unique to their creature; the raccoon siblings share bandit-mask / ringtail-swish / nimble-hand as secondary motifs only.

black-bear.notes: Black bear of forest and mountain: glossy black fur, tan muzzle; rakes bark with four claws, rears up to look big, licks honey and bluff-charges.

p.u0: Bear Swipe: four claw-rake scars rip off the edge stroke by stroke, pale wood at the root, white claw tips
p.u1: Stand Tall: black bears rear up on their hind legs along the edge, tan muzzles up, forepaws high

u2.n: Honey Lick: a paw comes up out of the comb dripping gold honey

u3.n: Huge Bluff: bears rear up and puff out from the edge in a bluff charge, dust kicked up

b0.n: Berry-Stained Rake: berry-purple claw scars rip off the edge, juice spots splattering

b1.n: Trouble Wallop: a heavy four-claw rake slams out and drops back

b2.n: Rear-Up Stance: bears stand up in a row along the edge, paw prints planted at their feet

b3.n: Shoulder Bowl: a rearing bear drops onto all fours and bowls out shoulder-first, rolling to the next piece

x0.n: Rolling Flop: bears flop off the edge and roll over in a cloud of dust

sloth-bear.notes: Sloth bear: a shaggy black coat with a pale chest V, long ivory claws for hooking, and a tube snout that hoovers termites with a loud huff.

p.u0: Long Claw Hook: long ivory sickle claws hook at spots along the edge, tied by a snag line

u1.n: Shaggy Charge: a shaggy black mane bursts off the edge at a run, dust flying

u2.n: Shaggy Mane: the long black coat bristles out like spikes, the pale chest V showing

p.u3: Sloth Hollow Nap: shaggy balls curled asleep rise out of a hollow, Zs drifting up

b0.n: Sloth Hook: long curved claws swing off the edge and hook shut

b1.n: Sloth Hoover: the pale tube snout pokes out and hoovers a stream of termites in; the chain sucks termites back along the edge

p.b2: Sloth Hollow: shaggy balls tuck into the edge and doze, breathing slowly

b3.n: Sloth Sniff: the snout slams out, huffs and snuffles back, termites flying in

x0.n: Sloth Swat: a long-clawed paw swats out and drops back

ice-bear.notes: Ice bear of the tundra: rimed white-blue fur and an icicle beard on its chin; it smashes floes, belly-slides on the ice and breathes fog.

u0.n: Rimed Coat: rimed fur bristles out in icicles with white tips, snow falling; the chain grows an icicle fringe

u1.n: Floe Smash: a white ice floe slab slams out, the blue crack splitting, chips flicking off

u2.n: Breath Fog: the white muzzle blows steaming fog clouds that spread out and drift back

u3.n: Snow Slide: the bear belly-slides the length of the edge, paws forward, ice streaks behind

b0.n: Frostbite Swipe: an icicle-bearded swipe flies off the edge, snow spraying

b1.n: Glazed Maul: an icy glazed paw slams out and back, a glint on the ice

p.b2: Snowdrift Heap: snowdrift mounds heap up along the edge, snow falling

b3.n: Skidding Bulk: the bulk skids out on its belly and bumps back, ice streaks

x0.n: Glaze Plough: a snow bank is ploughed up the length of the edge

glacier-bear.notes: Glacier bear: a rare silver-blue bear of ice fields; huge paws crack the glacier blue, its roar calves ice, its long shadow lies over the snow.

p.u0: Ice Paw: huge silver-blue paw prints stamp at spots, blue cracks tying them together; the chain cracks a crevasse print by print

u1.n: Blubber: thick fat humps line the edge and jiggle, soaking up the blow

u2.n: Glacier Roar: roaring heads open their jaws along the edge, roar arcs going out and ice chunks calving off

p.u3: Long Shadow: the bear's long dark shadow stretches out over the snow and slides back

b0.n: Glacier Rake: paw prints fly off the edge with cracks, snow falling

b1.n: Frozen Cuff: a huge paw slams out, stamps and cracks the ice

b2.n: Blue Ice Plant: paws plant along the edge and blue ice cracks spread under them

b3.n: Shadow Shove: a long shadow shoves out and snaps back

x0.n: Slow Sledge: the heavy body sledges along the edge, fat rolls wobbling

raccoon.notes: Raccoon of forest and wetland: a grey bandit with a black mask and ringed tail; clever little hands pry lids, grab loot and raid bins.

u0.n: Bandit Grab: little black hands grab at spots along the edge, tied by a loot line

u1.n: Scratch: spread little hands scratch off the edge, click marks

u2.n: Bin Lid: dented trash-can lids are held up along the edge and clang

p.u3: Clever Pry: a masked face slips along the edge peeking for a gap, eyes glinting

b0.n: Clever Paw Pinch: a quick hand pinches off the edge and drops crumbs

b1.n: Ringtail Wallop: the ringed tail swishes out and wallops back

b2.n: Masked Hunch: masked faces hunch down along the edge, only ears and glinting eyes showing

b3.n: Nimble Pocket-Dip: a hand dips in at spot after spot, quick as a pickpocket

x0.n: Trash-Lid Slam: a bin lid slams out and clangs down

crab-eating-raccoon.notes: Crab-eating raccoon of coast and mangrove: a browner, wet-furred bandit with a dark mask and a red crab in its paw; it dunks, washes and cracks its catch.

p.u0: Claw Snatch: a wet grey hand darts the length of the edge and snatches a red crab out of the water

u1.n: Shell Crack: crabs held in the paws crack open off the edge, white shards flying

u2.n: Dusk Cover: dark masks sink into the dusk haze, only eye glints showing

u3.n: Wash Off: wet fur shakes out and back, flinging fans of drops

b0.n: Tide Line Swipe: a wet ringed tail swipes off the edge along the tide line, foam bubbles

b1.n: Crab Clutch: hands clutch red crabs along the edge, dunking and lifting them

p.b2: Crab Masked Hunch: masked faces duck along the edge and peek

b3.n: Tide Shoulder: a wet shoulder barges out in a spray of drops

x0.n: Opening Swat: a wet hand swats out first, fingers spread

honey-badger-brute.notes: Honey badger brute: a low black body under a silver cape, utterly fearless; it charges anything, shrugs off bee stings and twists inside its loose skin.

p.u0: No Fear: bees dive at the silver cape and bounce off, bent stingers falling
p.u1: Brute Bite: the black-and-silver badger lunges off the edge jaws first, anger marks; the chain is a full charge round the edge

u2.n: Shrug Off: the badger twists round inside its loose skin and rises, the mantle staying put

u3.n: Mad Rush: the badger rams out head-down and bounces back, anger marks popping

b0.n: Badger Tear: badgers tear off the edge jaws open

b1.n: Badger Gouge: the badger gouges a furrow the length of the edge, dust behind

b2.n: Badger Hide: the loose silver hide holds along the edge while the body turns under it

b3.n: Badger Shrug: the caped hump shoves out and bees bounce off it

x0.n: Badger Frenzy: the badger whirls from spot to spot, jaws snapping

aardvark.notes: Aardvark: pale pink-grey, long ears and a tube snout; it digs burrows fast, smashes termite mounds and snuffles out ants.

u0.n: Burrow Claw: the snout shoves up out of a burrow mound and soil clods spray

u1.n: Mound Smash: clay termite mounds crack and burst, chunks and termites flying

p.u2: Snout Jab: the tube snout jabs the length of the edge, nose disc first, soil kicked up
p.u3: Ear Flap: long pink-lined ears flap open and fan out and back
p.b0: Burrow Dig: snouts dig off the edge out of fresh soil mounds, clods flying

b1.n: Burrow Smash: mound chunks are flung off the edge

p.b2: Burrow Hide: only the long ears stick up out of the burrow along the edge

b3.n: Burrow Snuffle: the snout pops out of hole after hole, snuffling

x0.n: Burrow Rip: a mound is ripped open along the edge, spires cracking one after another

giant-anteater.notes: Giant anteater of the rainforest: a long thin snout, a sticky tongue, huge foreclaws it walks on folded, and a banner of a tail it sleeps under like a cloak.

u0.n: Long Tongue: sticky pink tongues whip out at spots along the edge, tied by a thread of spit, ants stuck on

u1.n: Claw Hug: pale forepaws unfold their two huge claws off the edge and close in a hug

p.u2: Rear Up: the anteater rears up, huge claws raised in a row along the edge

u3.n: Tail Cloak: the great shaggy tail fans out like a spiky cloak; the chain sweeps it round the edge

b0.n: Foreclaw Rake: a huge foreclaw rakes out and drops back

b1.n: Sticky Tongue: the tongue flicks off the edge and back, ants stuck to it

b2.n: Cloak Curl: the tail curls along the edge like a cloak and sweeps slowly

b3.n: Snout Shove: the long snout shoves out, tongue flicking

x0.n: Cloaked Thrash: the tail thrashes off the edge in a sweep

beaver-foreman.notes: Beaver foreman of the wetland: brown fur, orange chisel teeth and a flat scaly tail it slaps on the water; it gnaws logs, builds the dam and calls its crew.

u0.n: Tail Slap: the flat scaly tail rises and slaps down, splash crowns and water rings; the chain slaps three times on the way

p.u1: Log Wall: sticks and logs stack crosswise into a dam along the edge, mud between

u2.n: Gnaw Through: orange teeth gnaw an hourglass notch through a log the length of the edge, chips flying

u3.n: Crew Call: round beaver crew heads bob up out of the water and rise, teeth showing

b0.n: Chisel Paw: chisel teeth chip at logs off the edge, sawdust falling

b1.n: Timber Wallop: a gnawed log swings out and thumps back

b2.n: Dam Buttress: the dam stacks up stick by stick along the edge, bubbles rising

b3.n: Crew Shove: the crew surfaces and shoves out together

x0.n: Flat Tail Slap: tails slap off the edge one after another, splash after splash
